nodes.label: Theorem 1.2 (a weighted condition on the support)
nodes.locator: Short paper Theorem 1.2, p. 2, label res:weighted-support
nodes.statement:
*Let $b\ge2$ be an integer, let $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}_{>0}$ be infinite, and let $P$ be a finite nonempty set of primes. Set $h(a)=\prod_{p\in P}p^{v_p(a)}$. If
$$


 W_{b,P}(A):=\sum_{a\in A}
 \frac{h(a)}{a(b^{h(a)}-1)}<\infty,
$$
then $X_A(b)$ is irrational. In particular, the base-two condition
$$


 \sum_{a\in A}\frac{h(a)}{a(2^{h(a)}-1)}<\infty
 \tag{W}
$$
implies that $X_A(b)$ is irrational for every integer $b\ge2$. Both conclusions are hereditary under passage to infinite subsets.*
nodes.boundary: The evidence mapping records a Lean statement that implies the printed one. Lean status per paper is kept in authored/evidence-status.json.

nodes.label: Theorem 3.1 (a summable divisor-cover criterion)
nodes.locator: Short paper Theorem 3.1, p. 6, label thm:variable-fractional-cover; Long record Theorem 1.3, p. 16, label thm:257-variable-fractional-cover
nodes.statement:
*For each $j\ge1$, let $F_j\subseteq\mathbb{N}_{>0}$ be finite, let $0<\alpha_j\le1$, and let $c_{j,d}\ge0$ satisfy
$$
f_{F_j}(n)^{\alpha_j}\le\sum_{d\mid n}c_{j,d}\quad(n\ge1).
$$
Set $C_j=\sum_{d\ge1}c_{j,d}/d$. If
$$

 \sum_{j\ge1}\frac{C_j2^{j\alpha_j}}{2^{\alpha_j}-1}<\infty,
 \tag{V}
$$
then $X_A(b)$ is irrational for every infinite $A\subseteq\bigcup_jF_j$ and every integer $b\ge2$.*
nodes.boundary: The evidence mapping records a Lean proof of exactly this statement. The evidence mapping records a Lean statement that implies the printed one. Lean status per paper is kept in authored/evidence-status.json.

nodes.label: The base comparison Δ_b ≤ Δ_2
nodes.locator: End of the proof of Theorem 3.1
nodes.statement: For $0\le r<d$ the function $(b^r-1)/(b^d-1)$ is nonincreasing on $b>1$. Hence $\Delta_{b,A}(N)\le\Delta_{2,A}(N)$ for every real $b\ge2$.
nodes.boundary: A step of the argument, written by Claude (Anthropic), an AI agent from the paper's own wording.

nodes.label: The choice of modulus
nodes.locator: Proof of Theorem 1.2, 'Choosing the modulus', p. 4
nodes.statement: With $p_*=\max P$ and $H\ge2p_*$, set $Q=L\prod_{p\in P}p^{\lfloor\log_pH\rfloor}$ and $G=\lfloor H/p_*\rfloor$. For $a\notin F$ with $h(a)\le H$ we have $h(a)\mid Q$, hence $(Q,a)\ge h(a)$; for $h(a)>H$ we have $(Q,a)\ge G$ instead.
nodes.boundary: A step of the argument, written by Claude (Anthropic), an AI agent from the paper's own wording.

nodes.label: The combined bound (5)
nodes.statement: $\frac1M\sum_{j=M}^{2M-1}\frac1{2^j}\sum_{t=1}^{2^j}\Delta_{b,A}(tQ)\le \varepsilon+\frac{2QW_{b,P}(A)}M+\frac{G(1+\log Q+2M\log2)+Q}{b^G-1}+4\,2^{-M}$, and with $F$ and $L$ fixed every term after $\varepsilon$ tends to zero as $H\to\infty$.
nodes.boundary: A step of the argument, written by Claude (Anthropic), an AI agent from the paper's own wording.

nodes.label: One distribution for both errors
nodes.statement: Both estimates use $\mathscr D_{Q;M,M}$ with $Q=L\prod_{p\in P}p^{\lfloor\log_pH\rfloor}$, $G=\lfloor H/\max P\rfloor$, $M=\lfloor2^{G/2}\rfloor$. Then $\mathscr D_{Q;M,M}(\Delta_{2,E}/\rho)<\frac18$ and $\mathscr D_{Q;M,M}S_J\le(1+4Q/M)K_J<\frac18$, so $\mathscr D_{Q;M,M}(\Delta_{2,E}/\rho+S_J)<\frac14$. This step uses only the linearity of the mean, and requires no independence between the two errors.
nodes.boundary: A step of the argument, written by Claude (Anthropic), an AI agent from the paper's own wording.

nodes.label: A divisor cover with no finite-prime weighted condition
nodes.statement: With odd primes $q_j\ge4^j$, disjoint prime sets $P_j$ and $V=\bigcup_{j\ge1}F_j$, $F_j=\{q_jd:d\mid M_j\}$: $\sum_{a\in V}1/a$ diverges, $V\notin\mathcal W_b$ for every integer $b\ge2$, and the choice $z_j=(j+S_j)^{-1}$, $\alpha_j=\log_2(1+z_j)$, $c_{j,q_jd}=z_j^{\omega(d)}$ makes the cover cost summable, so $V\in\mathcal C$.
nodes.boundary: A step of the argument, written by Claude (Anthropic), an AI agent from the paper's own wording.

nodes.label: A weighted support with no divisor cover
nodes.statement: With pairwise disjoint finite sets $P_k$ of odd primes such that $2^k/4\le S_k<2^k/4+1$ and $E=\bigcup_{k\ge1}\{2^kd:d\mid M_k\}$, the weighted sum for $P=\{2\}$ is finite, while $\mathbb E_{F_m}\log^+f_{F_m}\ge\frac{m-1}{8}\log2$. Thus $E\notin\mathcal C$.
nodes.boundary: A step of the argument, written by Claude (Anthropic), an AI agent from the paper's own wording.

nodes.label: One index controls every cover tail
nodes.statement: With allowances $t_j=\varepsilon2^{-j}$, choose $J$ with $K_J=\sum_{j>J}C_jt_j^{-\alpha_j}/(B_j-1)<1/4$ and $L$ divisible by every member of the first $J$ finite sets. For $M\ge4L$, (S) bounds the $\mathscr D_{L;R,M}$-mean of $S_J(N)=\sum_{j>J}t_j^{-\alpha_j}V_j(N)$ by $(1+4L/M)K_J<1/2$, so some sample satisfies $S_J(N)<1$, hence $U_j(N)<t_j$ for every $j>J$ and $0<\Delta_{2,A}(N)\le\sum_{j>J}U_j(N)\le\varepsilon$.
nodes.boundary: A step of the argument, written by Claude (Anthropic), an AI agent from the paper's own wording.

nodes.label: Divisor majorants and the cover condition (V)
nodes.statement: For each $j\ge1$, $F_j\subseteq\mathbb{N}_{>0}$ is finite, $0<\alpha_j\le1$, and $c_{j,d}\ge0$ satisfy $f_{F_j}(n)^{\alpha_j}\le\sum_{d\mid n}c_{j,d}$ $(n\ge1)$. With $C_j=\sum_{d\ge1}c_{j,d}/d$, condition (V) is $\sum_{j\ge1}\frac{C_j2^{j\alpha_j}}{2^{\alpha_j}-1}<\infty$.
nodes.boundary: A step of the argument, written by Claude (Anthropic), an AI agent from the paper's own wording.

nodes.label: Cyclotomic prime-power fact
nodes.statement: For a prime $\ell\mid\Phi_n(b)$ and $e=v_\ell(b^n-1)$, $\operatorname{ord}_{\ell^e}(b)=n$ for the full prime power $\ell^e$.
nodes.boundary: A step of the argument, written by Claude (Anthropic), an AI agent from the paper's own wording.

nodes.label: The displacement identity (D)
nodes.statement: For a positive integer $N$, $\Delta_{b,A}(N)=\sum_{a\in A}\frac{b^{N\bmod a}-1}{b^a-1}=(b^N-1)X_A(b)-J_{b,A}(N)$ with $J_{b,A}(N)=\sum_{a\in A,\,a\le N}\sum_{j=1}^{\lfloor N/a\rfloor}b^{N-ja}$. The identity follows on dividing $N$ by each $a$. At an integer base $J_{b,A}(N)$ is an integer.
nodes.boundary: A step of the argument, written by Claude (Anthropic), an AI agent from the paper's own wording.

nodes.label: Dominated convergence for a fixed modulus
nodes.statement: $\frac1X\sum_{m=1}^Xw_{b,d}(Qm)\le\frac{Q+2}{d}$. For this fixed $Q$ the majorant $(Q+2)/d$ is summable over $A$, so dominated convergence takes the limit in the observation length inside the sum over $d$ and gives the Cesàro mean $\sum_{d\in A}M_{Q,b}(d)$.
nodes.boundary: A step of the argument, written by Claude (Anthropic), an AI agent from the paper's own wording.

nodes.label: The dyadic estimate (4)
nodes.statement: For integers $Q,M\ge1$ and $\alpha_a\ge0$ with $\sum_a\alpha_a/a<\infty$, $\sum_{j=M}^{2M-1}\frac1{2^j}\sum_{a\le Q2^j}\alpha_a\le2Q\sum_{a\ge1}\frac{\alpha_a}{a}$; the estimate remains valid if the dyadic lengths start later.
nodes.boundary: A step of the argument, written by Claude (Anthropic), an AI agent from the paper's own wording.

nodes.label: The full support has displacements above 1/2
nodes.statement: $\Delta_{2,\mathbb{N}_{>0}}(N)>(2^N-1)\sum_{a>N}2^{-a}=1-2^{-N}\ge\frac12$ $(N\ge1)$. Erdős nevertheless proved the full-support value irrational [erdos1948].
nodes.boundary: A step of the argument, written by Claude (Anthropic), an AI agent from the paper's own wording.

nodes.label: The gcd-orbit mean (8)
nodes.statement: $M_{Q,b}(d):=\lim_{X\to\infty}\frac1X\sum_{m=1}^Xw_{b,d}(Qm)=\frac{g}{d(b^g-1)}\le\frac1d$, where $g=(Q,d)$.
nodes.boundary: A step of the argument, written by Claude (Anthropic), an AI agent from the paper's own wording.

nodes.label: The incidence form (6)
nodes.statement: $c_A(n)=\#\{a\in A:a\mid n\}$ and $X_A(b)=\sum_{n\ge1}c_A(n)b^{-n}$. This follows on expanding $(b^a-1)^{-1}=\sum_{j\ge1}b^{-aj}$ and interchanging the nonnegative sums.
nodes.boundary: A step of the argument, written by Claude (Anthropic), an AI agent from the paper's own wording.

nodes.label: The finite kernel estimate (S)
nodes.locator: Section 3, 'A finite mean for shifted divisor tails', estimate (S)
nodes.statement: For $1<B\le2$, positive integers $L,d,M$ and an integer $R\ge0$, with $w_{B,d}(n)=B^{n\bmod d}/(B^d-1)$: $\mathscr D_{L;R,M}w_{B,d}\le\frac{1+4L/M}{d(B-1)}$.
nodes.boundary: A step of the argument, written by Claude (Anthropic), an AI agent from the paper's own wording.

nodes.label: The lcm limit (9)
nodes.statement: With $Q_t=\operatorname{lcm}(1,\ldots,t)$, $\sum_{d\in A}M_{Q_t,b}(d)\longrightarrow X_A(b)$. Hence the limiting displacement means tend to zero.
nodes.boundary: A step of the argument, written by Claude (Anthropic), an AI agent from the paper's own wording.

nodes.label: The logarithmic obstruction (7)
nodes.statement: For every finite $F\subseteq\bigcup_jF_j$, $K\ge\mathbb E_F\Psi(f_F)\ge e\,\mathbb E_F\log^+f_F$, where $K=\sum_jC_j\eta_j^{-\alpha_j}/(2^{\alpha_j}-1)$ and $\Psi(t)=\inf_{0<\alpha\le1}t^\alpha/(2^\alpha-1)$.
nodes.boundary: A step of the argument, written by Claude (Anthropic), an AI agent from the paper's own wording.

nodes.label: The one-exponent orbit bound (2)
nodes.statement: Put $d_a(m)=(b^{m\bmod a}-1)/(b^a-1)$ and $g=(Q,a)$. Then $\frac1T\sum_{t=1}^T d_a(tQ)\le \frac{g}{a(b^g-1)}+\frac1{T(b^g-1)}$.
nodes.boundary: A step of the argument, written by Claude (Anthropic), an AI agent from the paper's own wording.

nodes.label: The outer bound (3)
nodes.statement: For $Y=QT$, $\frac1T\sum_{t=1}^T\sum_{a\in A,\,a>Y}d_a(tQ)\le\frac4T$, because $d_a(tQ)\le2\,2^{tQ-a}$ when $a>QT$ and $\sum_{t=1}^T2^{tQ-QT}\le2$.
nodes.boundary: A step of the argument, written by Claude (Anthropic), an AI agent from the paper's own wording.

nodes.label: The displacement is positive for infinite support
nodes.statement: For infinite $A$ the displacement $\Delta_{b,A}(N)$ is positive, because some $a\in A$ exceeds $N$.
nodes.boundary: A step of the argument, written by Claude (Anthropic), an AI agent from the paper's own wording.

nodes.label: The primes have displacements above 1/3
nodes.statement: Every prime singleton is admitted by both support criteria, and yet $\Delta_{2,\mathcal P}(N)>1/3$ for every $N\ge1$. Tao and Teräväinen nevertheless prove that $X_{\mathcal P}(2)$ is irrational.
nodes.boundary: A step of the argument, written by Claude (Anthropic), an AI agent from the paper's own wording.

nodes.label: Rationality forces displacements of at least 1/q
nodes.statement: If $X_A(b)=p/q$ with $p\in\mathbb Z$ and $q\ge1$ an integer, then $q\Delta_{b,A}(N)$ is a positive integer and $\Delta_{b,A}(N)\ge1/q$. It therefore suffices to find displacements tending to zero.
nodes.boundary: A step of the argument, written by Claude (Anthropic), an AI agent from the paper's own wording.

nodes.label: Subadditivity links the tails U_j and V_j
nodes.statement: With $B_j=2^{\alpha_j}$, $U_j(N)=\sum_{r\ge1}2^{-r}f_{F_j}(N+r)$ and $V_j(N)=\sum_{d\ge1}c_{j,d}w_{B_j,d}(N)$: $U_j(N)^{\alpha_j}\le\sum_{r\ge1}B_j^{-r}f_{F_j}(N+r)^{\alpha_j}\le\sum_{d\ge1}c_{j,d}\sum_{r\ge1,\,d\mid N+r}B_j^{-r}=V_j(N)$.
nodes.boundary: A step of the argument, written by Claude (Anthropic), an AI agent from the paper's own wording.

nodes.label: The cover displacement is at most the tail U_j
nodes.statement: For the displacement itself, the geometric-series identity gives $\Delta_{2,F_j}(N)=U_j(N)-X_{F_j}(2)\le U_j(N)$.
nodes.boundary: A step of the argument, written by Claude (Anthropic), an AI agent from the paper's own wording.

nodes.label: The unique-valuation step
nodes.locator: Appendix B, after Theorem B.1, p. 16
nodes.statement: Fix a divisibility-maximal $n\in F$ with $n\ge2$ and a prime $\ell\mid\Phi_n(b)$. Every other selected exponent $m$ satisfies $n\nmid m$, hence $v_\ell(b^m-1)<e$, so the $n$th summand has the uniquely smallest $\ell$-adic valuation and cannot cancel. Thus $\ell^e\mid D_F$ and $n\mid\operatorname{ord}_{D_F}(b)$.
nodes.boundary: A step of the argument, written by Claude (Anthropic), an AI agent from the paper's own wording.

nodes.label: Weighted sums decrease with the base and on subsets
nodes.locator: End of the proof of Theorem 1.2, p. 5
nodes.statement: Finally, $W_{b,P}(A)\le W_{2,P}(A)$ for $b\ge2$, and the weighted sum can only decrease when we pass to a subset.
nodes.boundary: A step of the argument, written by Claude (Anthropic), an AI agent from the paper's own wording.
